$what: connection:press-fit-tube-15 — the Ø15 arch cradle and the ring it holds, frozen from cecad.meshslice circle fits, cecad.meshfeatures.cylinders and cecad.meshfeatures.intervals on Pollen's meshes (metres, scale 1000), 2026-09-02, ce-designs/microduck lane T

host.frame: the mesh frame of motor_support.stl: x -39.5..34.0, y -26.2..28.0, z 0.4..19.2; the cradle axis is the x-line through (y 0, z 7.4995)

relief_d_basis.why_this_replaced_16.8: the value written here on 2026-09-02 was 16.8 — one decimal place in a file whose every other dimension carries four, and the house rule is 3–4 dp with the tolerance basis stated. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-03 (lane T fix pass) off the mesh VERTICES rather than off a ray, because a ray through a tessellated bore reads the facet, not the cylinder.
relief_d_basis.method: every vertex of motor_support.stl (scale 1000) with radius 8.30–8.50 mm about the cradle axis (y 0, z 7.4995) and x in -37.6..-36.4 — the relief band and nothing else. n = 64 vertices, in two rings of 32 at x -37.5000 and x -36.5000; no vertex row exists between them, so the surface is a straight cylinder over its whole length.
relief_d_basis.tolerance_basis: 1 sigma = 0.000247 mm on the diameter over 64 vertices; the full spread max-min is 0.0008 mm. That scatter is the STL’s float32 storage, not a shape: the design nominal is Ø16.8000 and the mesh carries it to +0.0007 mm.
relief_d_basis.why_a_ray_reads_less: the bore is a 32-facet chord polygon over the 152.4451° that exists; its vertices lie ON the cylinder and every facet lies INSIDE it by up to one sagitta, 0.00773 mm. A ray-cast caliper that crosses a facet near its centre therefore reads Ø16.7852, and cecad.meshslice.intervals() rounds its returns to 3 dp on top of that. An independent check on 2026-09-03 read r 8.3928 → Ø16.7856 at x -37.0 by exactly that route; it is the SAME surface measured through a chord, and it agrees with the mid-chord prediction to 0.0004 mm. The vertex figure is the one that describes the cylinder.
relief_d_basis.cross_check: the same vertex method on the Ø15 ring-band bore (r 7.45–7.55, x -39.8..-35.3, n = 124 at x -39.5000/-37.5000/-36.5000/-35.5000) reads Ø15.0007, sd 0.000237 — the same +0.0007 mm float32 offset from its own Ø15.0000 nominal, which is what makes the offset a storage artefact rather than a feature.
relief_d_basis.measured: 2026-09-03, cecad.meshslice.load + numpy on the mesh vertices; script out/laneT/remeasure_relief.py, output out/laneT/relief-remeasure.json

host.how_bands_were_read: cecad.meshfeatures.intervals(motor_support, axis x, y=0, z=15.6) — a line at radius 8.100 mm from the cradle axis, inside the Ø17.39 outer surface and outside the Ø15.0 bore: material exists only where the ring band exists
host.open_angle_why: 360 - 149.06: the arch is cut off flat at z 9.5000 and there is NO material below that plane at these x stations (cecad.meshslice section at x=-38.5 spans z 9.5000..16.1919 only). The cradle is a hook, not a bore.
host.arch_inner_arc_fits_superseded_by: vertex_remeasure_2026_09_03.cradle_bore — these are chord fits and read one half-sagitta (0.0039 mm) small.

placed_in_host_frame.how: the MJCF body/geom frames of robot_allcollisions.xml composed at zero pose, then expressed in the motor_support mesh frame (cecad.mjcf.bodies_world + quat_to_mat)

guest_journal.how_journal_span_was_read: cecad.meshfeatures.intervals(jaw, axis x) at (y 4.9, z 7.5) -> [-43.732, -37.0] (inside the Ø10 journal) and at (y 5.5, z 7.5) -> [-43.707, -39.7] (outside it): the journal proper is x -39.7000..-37.0000

coaxiality_mm.why: the cradle bore centre reads z 7.4995 (best station, residual mean 0.00352 mm) and the jaw journal centre reads z 7.5000 exactly (residual max 0.00254 mm) — the two PARTS are coaxial to 0.0005 mm. Pollen's MJCF places the bearing GEOM's axis at z 7.7000, 0.2005 mm above both, and 0.3000 mm outboard of the journal shoulder. That is a discrepancy in the visual placement of the model, not in the two parts' geometry, and it is recorded here rather than averaged away.

vertex_remeasure_2026_09_03.$what: EVERY DIAMETER IN THIS FILE RE-MEASURED OFF THE MESH VERTICES, 2026-09-03 (lane T fix pass, second round). It supersedes the meshslice cross-section fits recorded above wherever the two disagree.
vertex_remeasure_2026_09_03.why: An independent reader found that the headline bore Ø14.9938-14.9978 is the same facet-chord artefact this folder had already diagnosed for its Ø16.8 relief on 2026-09-02 and had not applied to its own headline number. cecad.meshslice's cross-section point set mixes facet CORNERS (which lie ON the design cylinder) with points interpolated along facet EDGES (which lie INSIDE it by up to one sagitta): each fit above reports n_pts 61 = 31 corners + 30 edge points, and with a facet step of 4.9176-4.9689 deg the sagitta is 0.00773 mm — half of it, 0.0039 mm, is exactly the shortfall from Ø15.0000. The reader is right and the correction is made here rather than argued with.
vertex_remeasure_2026_09_03.method: unique vertices of the binary STL (cecad.meshslice.load, scale 1000), selected by an x window and by radius about a SEED axis, then a circle fitted per x station with its CENTRE FREE (Kasa algebraic fit + 40 Gauss-Newton steps on the geometric residual, converged to |step| < 1e-14). residual_max is the largest distance of any vertex from that fitted circle: a residual at the 1e-6 mm level means every vertex lies on ONE circle, and that circle is the design cylinder. Script out/laneT/remeasure_bore_vertices.py (motor_support, jaw) and out/laneT/remeasure_bearing_od.py (the ring), output out/laneT/bore-vertex-remeasure.json and out/laneT/bearing-od-vertex-remeasure.json.
vertex_remeasure_2026_09_03.free_centre_matters: the centre must be FREE. The 2026-09-02 relief re-measurement took a mean radius about a FIXED seed axis at z 7.4995 — itself a chord-fit number — and read Ø16.8007. The vertex fit with a free centre reads Ø16.800000 and puts the axis at z 7.500000. Over an arc of 152.4451 deg centred on +z, a seed 0.0005 mm below the true axis biases the mean radius by 0.0005 x <cos> = 0.0005 x 0.7315 = 0.000366 mm, i.e. +0.00073 mm on the diameter — which is the whole of the +0.0007 mm that the 2026-09-02 row attributed to 'the STL's float32 storage'. THAT EXPLANATION IS REFUTED by this measurement: the same +0.0007 appeared on the Ø15 bore in that row's own cross-check for the same reason, because both were measured about the same wrong seed. float32 stores 15.0 exactly; the vertices carry it to 1.8e-7 mm.

cradle_bore.tolerance_basis: all four stations return the identical fit to 8 dp (Ø15.00000018, centre z 7.499999907). The spread across stations is 0.0 mm; the spread WITHIN a station is 0.0000007 mm, which is the float32 storage of the STL. The design nominal is Ø15.0000 and the mesh carries it to 1.8e-7 mm.
cradle_bore.supersedes: arch_inner_arc_fits above (Ø14.9938 / 14.9954 / 14.9978 and the two outlier stations Ø15.0121 / 15.0179): those are chord fits, one half-sagitta small, and the two outliers are end-cap stations where the section picks up the chamfer.

cradle_relief.supersedes: relief_d_mm 16.8007 and relief_d_basis above — right method, wrong axis.

cradle_outer.supersedes: arch_outer_arc_fit Ø17.3926 (residual max 0.02627) — the same chord artefact, larger here because the fit also swallowed the fillet at the arch's feet.

jaw_journal.supersedes: journal_arc_fits' 'residual max 0.00254 mm'. That number was the INSTRUMENT's residual, not the surface's: the vertices lie on one circle to 0.00000055 mm.

ring_od.why_re_measured_here: so that the cradle/ring comparison is like-for-like. Comparing a vertex-measured ring against a chord-measured cradle is what produced the phantom interference. The ring's bore reads Ø10.000000 at z 0.2000/2.8000 and Ø10.399999 at the two chamfered end faces.

fit_result.what_it_means: LINE-TO-LINE. Zero clearance and zero interference, both sides measured the same way. The published claim of '0.0000-0.0062 mm of nominal interference' and compat.py's printed diametral_gap_mm -0.0062 describe an interference that does not exist. The folder's VERDICT does not change — an arch open over 210.94 deg cannot grip at any interference — but the number was wrong and is corrected.

coaxiality_mm.why: 0.000000031 mm apart, which is below both fits' own residual (7.0e-7 and 5.5e-7 mm). The honest statement is COAXIAL to better than 0.0000010 mm — bounded by the instrument, not resolved by it. This supersedes the 0.0005 mm above, which was the difference between two CHORD-fit centres (z 7.4995 vs z 7.5000) and not a real offset. The 0.2005 mm by which Pollen's MJCF places the bearing GEOM above the axis becomes 0.2000 mm on the same correction and still stands as a placement artefact of the visual model.
